note: Dated, owned exceptions to Tier 1 conformance rules. R-VER-3: 'a static key requires a documented exception with an expiry date.' An exception with no `expires` is NOT honoured — the finding stays a failure and says why. On expiry the finding returns as a failure naming the owner and how many days it is overdue. Every report prints the live exceptions and the days remaining, so a deferral stays visible instead of becoming the new normal.
howToAdd: rule + path + reason + owner + approved + expires. All six required. Never add one to quiet a report you have not read.

The key is NOT in the deploy path and touches no product infrastructure. PREFERRED FIX, which removes the need for this exception entirely: move the file out of G:\My Drive\Caspr\ into a password manager now. That satisfies R-CTX-1 immediately without touching the rotation schedule, because the file's LOCATION and the key's ROTATION are separable problems.
exceptions.expiryNote: PLACEHOLDER — 90 days, not the real cutover date, which was not known when this was written. Replace with the actual new.caspr.ai -> caspr.ai date. If cutover slips past this, the finding returns as a failure, which is the intended behaviour: an exception that outlives its justification is a rule that was quietly deleted.
exceptions.residualRisk: The file remains readable by every session in this project and remains replicated to Google Drive for the life of this exception. Under R-RSP-3 the value should already be considered compromised, so the exception defers remediation of a known exposure rather than accepting an unknown one.
